changelog.change: Registered the wordle generator: 6-ezhuthu answers, 8 attempts, three bands separated on familiarity alone, and a two-rung ladder.
changelog.why: Row 19 - the third Game, and the first whose knobs were set by simulating the game rather than by porting a convention. attempts is 8 and it is the load-bearing number. Modelled against a player who guesses a familiar word still consistent with every mark so far, a 6-ezhuthu board is solved within 8 guesses 94.5 percent of the time on the easy band, 93.5 on medium and 85.5 on hard - against 86.2 / 84.5 / 71.5 at seven. Seven is the N+1 the English wordles use and it would lose better than one hard day in four, and a hard day is one slot of every three. Tamil earns the extra row honestly: its alphabet is 247 ezhuthu against English's 26, 203 of them are in play in this set, and the best fixed opening word among 400 candidates averages 1.13 marks a game where a good English opener averages about two. Narrowing the hard band to drop the rarest quarter was measured as the alternative and REJECTED: q3 alone solves 75.0 percent within 7 and q4 alone 74.0, so the quarter costs a quarter of the vocabulary and buys one point - once the length is pinned, what decides whether a board is winnable is information per guess, not how rare the answer is. The bands are therefore all 6 to 6 and separate on maxStratum alone, which is the honest shape once the width is fixed: with one width the only thing left that makes a word hard is how well the player knows it, and the set splits 1,540 / 1,540 / 3,080 across the bands so every one of them fills. reveal stays 0 - handing over the first ezhuthu would be the strongest hint in the game given away for nothing, and this ladder deliberately refuses to sell even that. The ladder is two rungs: firstEzhuthu is refused because the player can buy the same fact by spending a guess, and one guess answers five other positions at the same time, so the rung is strictly worse than the move it competes with. choiceCount is untouched and unread - there is no bank in this Game; the keyboard is a composer over the 247-ezhuthu inventory, which is a fact about Tamil rather than a per-puzzle knob. categoryLabels is restated rather than shared because hint wording is per-Game by contract.

changelog.change: Registered the missing-letters generator, and gave a difficulty band a blanks count and a Game a choiceCount.
changelog.why: Row 18 - the second Game, and the first proof that adding one is a registry entry plus a payload builder rather than a rewrite of the day loop. Both new knobs carry defaults that leave every day baked before them valid and the anagram's entry untouched. blanks sits on the BAND because hiding a second ezhuthu is a difficulty dial and the bands are where difficulty is declared; it is the honest way to make a band harder, since it multiplies the guess space instead of reaching for a rarer word, and the contract refuses a band that could hide every ezhuthu of its shortest word. It is 2 only on hard, and hard starts at five ezhuthu, because measured over the 25,210-row served set a two-blank mask has a single answer for 96.7 percent of five-ezhuthu words and 100 percent of six, against 42.0 percent at four. choiceCount is a real balance number rather than a layout preference: there is no Tamil keyboard in this game, so the bank is how a hidden ezhuthu is entered at all, and its size is the odds a player who knows nothing still guesses right inside the allowed attempts - 8 puts that at 3 in 8 for a one-blank puzzle and 3 in 56 for a two-blank one. The ladder is two rungs, not three: firstEzhuthu cannot be sold here because this board has already printed every ezhuthu it is not hiding, so the rung is either a fact on the screen or the answer itself. categoryLabels is restated rather than shared because hint wording is per-Game by contract - it lives beside the templates - and this Game's is identical today only because nothing has asked it to differ.

changelog.change: Rebuilt the hint ladder: deleted the length rung, added a category rung at cost 1 and a meaning rung at cost 3 either side of the existing first-ezhuthu rung at cost 2, and added categoryLabels holding the Tamil tag the category rung renders for each lexicon category slug.
changelog.why: Row 14 of the lexicon pipeline - the length rung charged one point for the tile count already on the player's screen, and offering it as one of two hints short-changed the player. The ladder is walked in order rather than chosen from, so its order is its pricing and the three rungs now escalate in what they return as well as in what they cost: a tag, then a letter, then a phrase. categoryLabels lives here rather than in copy.json because hint wording lives here - the Tamil templates already do - and the lexicon's categories column holds English slugs, since a category is a machine dimension there. A slug with no label has no rung: a ladder that is sometimes two rungs is correct.

changelog.change: Added themeEveryNDays and gave the anagram generator its first themed wordlist.
changelog.why: Row 15 of the lexicon pipeline - a themed set nothing draws from is a dataset nobody reads, so the day loop needs a place to find one. A theme is registered per Game beside its ordinary wordlist, and the day runs it only when a whole playlist can be drawn from it. themeEveryNDays is 7 because the theme is wide enough to fill months of consecutive days, and a Daily that is nature every day for a season is the opposite of the variety a theme exists to add; one themed day a week is also the cadence the theme's growth target was sized against.

changelog.change: Gave every difficulty band a maxStratum bound alongside its length bounds, and moved the length bounds to 3-4 easy, 4-5 medium, 5-6 hard.
changelog.why: Row 12 of the lexicon pipeline - difficulty is two-axis, because length alone is anti-correlated at both tails: a long Tamil headword is usually a compound that decomposes and is easier than its tile count suggests, while a short rare word is brutal. The old easy band was minLength 3 / maxLength 3, which forced the generator into the shortest words - disproportionately literary, and brute-forceable at six arrangements against three attempts. Bounding easy to the most familiar quarter is also what makes it impossible for a day to be three words nobody knows.

changelog.change: Initial daily-engine registry: the anagram generator, its difficulty bands, and its hint wording.
changelog.why: Row 13 - the daily puzzle engine is a separate layer from the corpus, so its knobs are a separate file from the runtime app config.
